subject: Spanish - Foreign Language

outcomes.text: Use Spanish nouns with correct gender and singular or plural forms.
Use definite and indefinite articles, including contractions such as al and del, and lo with adjectives.
Use adjectives with appropriate agreement, position, demonstrative forms and possessive forms.
Use common adverbs and adverbial expressions for manner, time, place and degree.
Form comparisons and superlatives, including irregular forms and very strong adjective or adverb forms.
Use subject, object, reflexive, possessive, relative and demonstrative pronouns appropriately.
Use common indefinite adjectives and pronouns to express quantities, people, objects and alternatives.
Form questions using Spanish interrogative words for information about people, places, time, quantity, manner and reasons.
Use regular, irregular, reflexive and stem-changing verbs in all persons, including negative and impersonal constructions.
Use ser, estar, tener, weather verbs and common expressions with gustar and similar verbs.
Use present, past, future, conditional, perfect, pluperfect and continuous tenses accurately.
Use gerunds, the passive voice and common imperative forms.
Use present and imperfect subjunctive forms for commands, wishes, emotions, purpose, future time and hypothetical situations.
Use common Spanish prepositions, including the personal a.
Join ideas using coordinating and subordinating conjunctions such as y, o, pero, porque, cuando, mientras and si.
Use cardinal and ordinal numbers, fractions, quantities, dates, clock times and desde hace constructions.
Understand and use common Spanish adjectives describing qualities, feelings, size, condition, opinions and other familiar characteristics.
Understand and use common adverbs and prepositions expressing place, possibility, frequency, manner, emphasis and degree.
Understand and use cardinal and ordinal numbers, fractions and other common expressions involving quantity and frequency.
Understand and use common verbs for actions, communication, movement, feelings, thoughts, possession, daily routines and social interaction.
Learn vocabulary for educational institutions, from nursery and primary school through secondary school and university.
Learn vocabulary for learners, courses, academic years, departments, staff, education, school facilities and students.
Learn vocabulary for classroom equipment and learning tools, including stationery, books, desks, paper, boards and dictionaries.
Learn vocabulary for school subjects, including sciences, languages, humanities, arts, computing, mathematics, sport and religion.
Learn vocabulary for lessons, classmates, homework, exercises, examinations, questions, projects, tests, grades and results.
Use verbs and expressions for studying, understanding, answering, writing, reading, revising, taking notes, passing and failing.
Learn vocabulary for a wide range of occupations and professions, including trades, services, public roles, healthcare and education.
Learn vocabulary for workplaces, employers, employees, organisations, jobs, businesses, salaries, unemployment and industrial action.
Use expressions for acting, finding or losing work, hiring, earning, retiring, starting a business, promotion, dismissal and applications.
Use Spanish expressions for sequence, duration, frequency, parts of the day, clock times, dates and days.
Use Spanish vocabulary for weekdays and weekends.
Use Spanish vocabulary for months, years and dates.
Use Spanish vocabulary for the four seasons.
Name common forms of transport, travel items and transport-related places in Spanish.
Identify and discuss meals, snacks and dietary choices in Spanish.
Name common fruits and vegetables in Spanish.
Name common meat, fish and seafood items in Spanish.
Name additional foods and ingredients in Spanish.
Name common snack foods in Spanish.
Name common drinks and describe beverages in Spanish.
Use Spanish verbs and expressions for eating, drinking and preparing food.
Describe food using Spanish adjectives for taste, freshness and preparation.
Name common cutlery, crockery and cooking utensils in Spanish.
Name major parts of the body in Spanish.
Use Spanish verbs and expressions relating to the senses and bodily actions.
Identify Spanish vocabulary for healthcare professionals, facilities and medicines.
Discuss illness, injuries, symptoms, treatment and healthy activities in Spanish.
Discuss leisure activities including music, reading, television, films, concerts and festivals.
Discuss hobbies involving music, art, photography, gardening, games, reading and instruments.
Name sports, sporting equipment, venues, participants and competitive activities in Spanish.
Use Spanish verbs and expressions for travelling, driving, directions and journeys.
Name common transport types, travel documents, luggage, tickets, vehicles and travel facilities.
Discuss travelling, walking, driving, parking, directions, boarding, arrival and delays in Spanish.

subtopics.title: Las personas y los lugares – Los continentes

outcomes.text: Name the continents and major geographical regions in Spanish.

subtopics.title: El entorno edificado – Las zonas urbanas

outcomes.text: Learn vocabulary for urban areas, roads, transport infrastructure, traffic, crossings, neighbourhoods and public spaces.
Learn vocabulary for natural features, environmental issues, resources, landscapes, weather-related nature and environmental protection.
Use verbs and expressions for helping, protecting, changing, conserving, reducing, reusing and addressing environmental problems.
Learn vocabulary for common animals, including domestic, wild and farm animals.

subtopics.title: El mundo natural y el medio ambiente – El clima y el tiempo

outcomes.text: Learn vocabulary for temperature, seasons, weather conditions and extreme weather phenomena.

subtopics.title: El entorno edificado – Los edificios y los servicios

outcomes.text: Learn vocabulary for public, educational, medical, leisure, transport, hospitality and other local buildings and services.
Learn vocabulary for shops, shopping locations, customers, staff, prices, payment, opening status and retail goods.
Use expressions for buying, paying, shopping, renting, returning goods, requesting refunds, complaining and asking prices.
Learn units for measuring weight, distance, volume and length.
Use vocabulary describing size, height and length.
Use vocabulary for circular, square and triangular shapes.
Learn vocabulary for common materials, including cotton, leather, glass, wool, wood, metal, paper, plastic, gold and silver.
Use common Spanish greetings, farewells, apologies, thanks and conversational phrases.
Use Spanish exclamations to express welcome, interest, annoyance, regret and admiration.
Invite people, respond to invitations and express willingness or desire to participate.
Name family members and describe family structures, relationships and personal circumstances.
Discuss birth, upbringing, marriage, adoption, death, residence and personal details in Spanish.
Describe people’s physical appearance, age, build, hair, eyes, clothing and distinguishing features.
Describe personality, emotions, moods and attitudes using Spanish adjectives.
Use Spanish verbs and expressions for affection, reactions, feelings and emotional responses.
Name rooms, structural features and household furniture in Spanish.
Name common objects and furniture found in a living room.
Name bathroom items and personal care products in Spanish.
Describe washing, bathing, grooming and other bathroom routines in Spanish.
Name common kitchen containers, surfaces and equipment in Spanish.
Discuss cooking, cleaning, heating, freezing and preparing meals in Spanish.
Name common bedroom furniture and objects in Spanish.
Describe sleeping, waking, going to bed, resting and feeling tired in Spanish.
Discuss common household chores and cleaning activities in Spanish.
Name common garden features, plants and outdoor objects in Spanish.
Describe gardening, cultivating plants and planting flowers or vegetables in Spanish.
Name common household appliances and domestic utilities in Spanish.
Discuss operating, repairing, opening, closing and switching household appliances in Spanish.
Name and describe a range of colours in Spanish.
Name clothing, footwear and accessories, and describe their style, size and appearance.
Discuss wearing, trying on, removing, choosing and fitting clothes in Spanish.
Learn vocabulary for digital devices, online services, files, applications, communication, media and internet safety.
Use verbs and expressions for copying, downloading, finding, sending, saving, browsing, publishing and uploading digital content.
Learn vocabulary for documents, written texts, publications, forms, certificates, letters, notices and printed materials.

subtopics.title: Los países, las nacionalidades y los idiomas

outcomes.text: Describe a learner’s mother tongue, other studied languages, nationality, country of residence and Spanish-speaking countries.

subtopics.title: La cultura – las costumbres, las creencias y las celebraciones

outcomes.text: Learn vocabulary for celebrations, religious beliefs, festivals, national occasions, Christmas traditions, birthdays, weddings and places of worship.
Use expressions for celebrating, believing, having faith and describing religious identity.
